newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London flat in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London flat in quiet trade.

text.p: Japanese stocks in London were little changed on Wednesday as investors took their cue from the quiet Tokyo share market and mulled over this month's elections in Japan, dealers said.

"The market is well supported but, unless we get some major news -- perhaps a big jump on the dollar/yen front or dramatic figures from the U.S. to revive the rates debate, we won't see much change before the elections," one dealer said.
In London the Nikkei 50 index was up 1.28 points at 1,468.54 in mid-afternoon trading after the Nikkei 225 Average gained 0.17 percent in Tokyo to close at 21,498.60 points.

"We think the market is waiting for the Nikkei to get up to 22,000 points before taking profits. But for the moment, given the rates outlook and the elections, people are content to sit on their hands," the trader said.
Dealers said there was some interest in blue chips.
Banks, notably Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Bank, picked up slightly after weakening in Tokyo, they said.
Mitsubishi Oil gained in Tokyo on the back of an oil discovery in Papua New Guinea but was steady in London.
